Streaming is choppy. i am getting faces that are just disappearing their material when im looking right at it. i think the problem is you are taking LoS first before distance when distance should trump LoS and LoS should be a after distance so that far things dont draw
let me show u example

this building i have arrows pointed at the face not in render [Image #1] 

[Image #2] now its in render. but i just had to walk a fuck load of distance to make that happen when i saw it the whole time, and the other face was always in render also and it shows up

resolution: Fixed all three streaming defects the user caught live, one root: the LOD shell. (1) FACE-EATER (brick face vanishing while standing next to it, ~1m brick strip left at the bottom): the draw-range gap-merge bridged LOD ranges ACROSS a resident chunk, drawing its merged dark LOD box over the live textured detail — the bottom strip was the 4% LOD shrink lifting the box off the ground; range coalescing is now contiguous-only (never bridges an occupied-but-unwanted chunk) with a counted warn-once overflow instead of range-widening. (2) PHANTOM BUILDING filling a real gap: the quadrant union-AABB LOD invented mass between separate buildings; the shell is now VERBATIM copies of real rows — a far building is its own exact box in its own color (material rows copy their fallback color before whitening, so brick reads brick-ish at any distance), nothing merged or shrunk; survivors picked by a height ladder auto-raised to fit the GPU budget (user map keeps everything >=2m; 512-block lab keeps the >=16m skyline). (3) WALK-A-LOT before a face textures: promotion radius now scales with chunk content height (6 m-per-meter, the era's per-model draw distance — an 80m tower textures from ~480m). Draw order was already distance-then-sight as the user suspected it should be; these were LOD-tier defects masquerading as ordering. 4 unit tests green incl. the bridge regression; rjit game verify GREEN 73/73; massive lab submits ~5% of 776k rows/frame in 213 draws. User should rebuild + replay to confirm the brick building stays put.
